text:
sara: quick follow-up from the FP8/INT8 transpose-handling RFC — want to align on runtime semantics for scaling + rounding when we move transposes across quant boundaries. TL;DR: there are correctness vs perf tradeoffs we didn’t fully settle in the doc.

anya: agree, saw a few edgecases in the canary where late-token drift popped up when we applied per-tensor scaling after transpose.

michael: short note: two main design choices i see — (A) pretranspose-scaling: apply scale factors before doing the transpose so quantized math uses already-scaled values, or (B) posttranspose-scaling: keep integer layout stable and scale after transpose. each has perf/accuracy tradeoffs.

kevin: also need to pick a default rounding mode. stochastic rounding helps fp8 drift but costs determinism / perf. bankers/nearest-even is fast and deterministic.

anya: observed behaviour in canary: using posttranspose-scaling + nearest-even caused small bias that accumulates in multihead attention softmax inputs for longctx. drift ~0.2-0.5% on Rouge-L in that slice.

michael: interesting. do we have a cheap mitigation? per-channel scale on weight rows + pretranspose-scaling maybe reduces bias but adds a memory stride/transpose penalty.

sara: proposal: runtime default = pretranspose-scaling + per-tensor nearest-even; canary option = pretranspose-scaling + per-channel stochastic for customers opting in. also expose a header/config so customers can explicitly request posttranspose semantics if they need int8 legacy behaviour.

anya: +1 to exposing header. operationally we need a clear fallback: if per-channel metadata missing, default to per-tensor path.

michael: +1 but we should add a low-overhead fastpath for pretranspose per-channel that avoids a full copy when stride-friendly (e.g., when dims align). that keeps perf good for common shapes.

kevin: implementation detail: accumulation during matmul should still use int32 or fp16 acc depending on hardware. For fp8 paths we do fp16 accumulate. For int8 we keep int32 accumulate — otherwise we see dynamic range explosion. document that in runtime contract.

anya: test plan idea: add a small harness that computes forward for 3 variants (pre/post scale) × (per-tensor/per-channel) × (nearest/stochastic) for 1000 prompts and compare tokenwise logits, softmax KL, and downstream evals. cheap shadow sampling.

michael: perf bench owners: i'll run microbench for the pretranspose fastpath vs naive copy on A100 and L4. want p99 latency and throughput curves.

sara: config API sketch:
```yaml
quantization:
  precision_profile: "fp8_prefer" # fp8_prefer | int8_compat | mixed
  transpose_semantics: "pretranspose-scaling" # pretranspose-scaling | posttranspose-scaling
  scaling: # runtime hints
    mode: "per_channel" # per_channel | per_tensor
    rounding: "nearest_even" # nearest_even | stochastic | bankers
```

kevin: + add note: rounding:stochastic should be opt-in for hosted canary only, not default. otherwise we break reproducibility for users.

deploy-bot: canary-check triggered for precision-profiles branch — smoke tests running. :gear:

anya: one more nuance: when switching precision mid-sequence (e.g., kv-cache from fp16 -> fp8 for later tokens) need explicit handshake metadata so client and runtime agree on where scaling switches. without it we misalign under longctx. add a token-indexed marker in kv header.

michael: good catch. add small header field: kv_precision_boundary_idx. runtime will validate and return 4xx + diagnostics if mismatch.

sara: action items:
- anya: implement prototype for pretranspose per-channel fastpath + test harness (owner)
- michael: perf microbench on A100/L4 and add p99 curves (owner)
- kevin: add docs for accumulate semantics + rounding recommendations (owner)
- sara: update RFC with defaults, header contract, and canary gating plan (owner)

anya: will start prototype tomorrow, posting PR to repo/quant-runtime.

michael: i'll queue perf runs after lunch.

kevin: drafting docs, will ping for review.

sara: thanks all — if canary smoke passes, i'll flip the RFC status to "implementation pending" and schedule a short sync with eng-infra to wire the header validation. :+1:

deploy-bot: canary-check passed on unit-smoke, regression-suite running (logs at https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/9876).
